# Temple Scroll Column 56 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 56 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**56:1** You shall not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.

**56:2** When brothers live together and one of them dies without a son, the widow shall not marry outside the family to a stranger; her husband's brother shall go to her and take her as his wife and perform the duty of a brother-in-law for her.

**56:3** The firstborn son she bears shall carry on the name of the dead brother, so that his name will not be blotted out from Israel.

**56:4** But if the man is not willing to marry his brother's wife, she shall go up to the gate before the elders and say: My husband's brother refuses to carry on his brother's name in Israel; he will not perform the duty of a brother-in-law for me.

**56:5** The elders of his city shall summon him and speak to him; and if he stands firm and says: I am not willing to marry her —

**56:6** then his brother's wife shall approach him in the presence of the elders, pull his sandal off his foot, spit in his face, and declare: This is what is done to the man who will not build up his brother's house.

**56:7** And his family shall be known in Israel as the House of the Unsandaled.

**56:8** If two men are fighting with each other, and the wife of one of them intervenes to rescue her husband from the one who is striking him, and she reaches out her hand and seizes his private parts —

**56:9** you shall cut off her hand; show her no pity.

**56:10** You shall not have in your bag two different weights, one heavy and one light.

**56:11** You shall not have in your house two different measures, one large and one small.

**56:12** You shall have only a full and honest weight; you shall have only a full and honest measure, so that your days may be prolonged in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.

**56:13** For everyone who does such things, everyone who acts dishonestly, is an abomination to the LORD your God.

**56:14** When you come to the land that I am giving you, and you possess it and settle in it, and you say: I will set a king over me, like all the nations around me —

**56:15** you shall surely set over you a king whom I shall choose. From among your brothers you shall set a king over you; you may not set over you a foreign man who is not your brother.

**56:16** Only he shall not acquire many horses for himself, and he shall not send the people back to Egypt to acquire more horses, for I have said to you: You shall never go back that way again.

**56:17** And he shall not acquire many wives for himself, lest his heart turn aside; nor shall he acquire for himself excessive silver and gold.

**56:18** When he sits on the throne of his kingdom, they shall write for him a copy of this Torah on a scroll, from the one that is before the priests.

**56:19** It shall remain with him, and he shall read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God by keeping all the words of this Torah and these statutes, and doing them,

**56:20** so that his heart may not be lifted up above his brothers, and so that he may not turn aside from the commandment, either to the right or to the left, in order that he may continue long in his kingdom, he and his sons, in the midst of Israel.

**56:21** He shall not [...] the inheritance of any tribe, for each shall hold fast to his own inheritance.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 56 reworks Deuteronomy 25:4-17:20. The levirate marriage law uses "duty of a brother-in-law" (yibbum) as the standard legal rendering. The Law of the King (56:14-21) is the Temple Scroll's most distinctive legal section, with God speaking in first person: "whom I shall choose." The prohibition on multiplying horses, wives, and wealth follows Deuteronomy 17:16-17 closely.*
